# What `async` and `defer` do on `<script>`

## Default: a classic external script with no attributes
A plain `<script src="…">` stops the parser. The WHATWG spec says: "If neither attribute is present, then the script is fetched and evaluated immediately, blocking parsing until these are both complete." (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html)

## `defer` on a classic external script
- **Parsing:** the script downloads while the parser keeps going. The spec says it "will be fetched in parallel and evaluated when the page has finished parsing" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).
- **Timing vs DOMContentLoaded:** it runs after parsing finishes and before DOMContentLoaded. MDN says the script runs "after the document has been parsed, but before firing DOMContentLoaded event," and that deferred scripts "will prevent the DOMContentLoaded event from firing until the script has loaded and finished evaluating" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). MDN's DOMContentLoaded page agrees: the event fires once parsing is done and all deferred scripts have downloaded and run (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event).
- **Order:** guaranteed to be document order. In the spec's algorithm, each deferred script is appended to a single per-document *list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing* (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). MDN states the order directly (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).

## `async` on a classic external script
- **Parsing:** the script downloads while the parser keeps going, then runs "as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes)" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). Running it does occupy the page: MDN says async execution "blocks the page and does not guarantee any specific execution order" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).
- **Order:** none is guaranteed. The spec puts async scripts in a *set* of scripts that will execute as soon as possible, and each one runs when its own result is ready (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). MDN: "You can't rely on the order the scripts will load in."
- **Timing vs DOMContentLoaded:** DOMContentLoaded doesn't wait for async scripts (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event). The spec's "potentially before parsing completes" means an async script can run before or after the event.

**Where the sources disagree:**
- MDN's DOMContentLoaded page says the event fires "before the execution of scripts with async." It also says an async-included script will find that DOMContentLoaded "has already fired." Both statements are stronger than the spec, which allows an async script to run before parsing finishes. The cautious reading is that the order is not guaranteed either way.
- web.dev says deferred scripts run "at the same time as" DOMContentLoaded (https://web.dev/learn/performance/optimize-resource-loading). The spec and MDN are more precise: deferred scripts run first, then the event fires.
- MDN's own summary says deferred scripts run "once everything has finished loading." That is looser than its attribute reference, which says after parsing and before DOMContentLoaded.

## Both `async` and `defer` set
`async` wins. MDN says the element acts "as if only the async attribute is specified." The spec says you may still add `defer` so that old browsers that only support `defer` fall back to it instead of blocking (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

## Inline classic scripts
On a classic script without `src`, `async` and `defer` are not allowed and do nothing (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). The spec's attribute table marks both as not allowed for inline classic scripts. Its algorithm only uses the async/defer branches when the script is classic with a `src`, or is a module. An inline classic script normally runs immediately and blocks the parser. One exception: if a parser-inserted script is waiting on a style sheet that blocks scripts, it becomes the pending parsing-blocking script and runs once that style sheet loads (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). web.dev: "inline scripts block the parser until the script is parsed and executed."

## `type="module"`
- **Default:** deferred, whether external or inline. The module and its dependencies are fetched while parsing continues and run when parsing has finished. In the spec, modules go into the same deferred list as `defer` scripts, so they run in document order alongside them and before DOMContentLoaded. MDN's DOMContentLoaded page lists `<script type="module">` among the deferred scripts the event waits for.
- **`defer`:** has no effect on modules, according to the spec and MDN.
- **`async`:** the module and all its dependencies are fetched in parallel, and the module runs as soon as it is available, possibly before parsing completes. Unlike inline classic scripts, inline modules do respect `async`. The spec's table allows `async` on inline modules, and web.dev notes that inline modules are also deferred automatically.

## Two notes on sources
- The WHATWG parsing page (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html) returned 404. I couldn't quote the spec's "the end" steps, so the DOMContentLoaded timing above relies on MDN plus the scripting chapter.
- Some spec sentences in the plan weren't on the page word for word, for example "For classic scripts, if the async attribute is present". The current text says "For external classic scripts…". I quoted the actual wording.
